title: Powys to receive string of cycling hubs as part of £4.5m Tour de France funding

POWYS is set to benefit from a major investment in cycling tourism as part of a £4.5 million Welsh Government programme linked to the Tour de France Grand Départ in 2027. A key part of the funding package will see £100,000 invested in a network of cycling hubs across Powys, with facilities planned for Welshpool, Newtown, Machynlleth, Llandrindod Wells and Llanfyllin. The North Powys Cycle Hubs project, being delivered by Powys County Council, will provide secure cycle parking, repair stations, bike-wash facilities, e-bike charging points and visitor information to support both local riders and visitors. The funding is intended to help cyclists explore more of Mid Wales, including attractions such as Powis Castle, which will form part of the Powys leg for next year's Tour de France Grand Depart. (Image: Golley Slater.) The hubs are intended to help cyclists explore more of Mid Wales, including attractions such as Powis Castle and the National Cycle Museum , while encouraging greater footfall and spending in local communities. The Powys scheme forms part of a wider £3.19 million package being shared between 54 cycling tourism projects across Wales. A further £1.3 million will also be made available through a new fund helping businesses and community organisations improve facilities for cyclists. The investment comes as Wales prepares to host the opening stages of the Tour de France in 2027, with Visit Wales also planning to make 2027 the 'Year of Cycling'. Cabinet secretary for enterprise, connectivity and energy, Adam Price, said: "The Tour de France Grand Départ presents a once-in-a-generation opportunity for Wales. "From coastal routes and community cycling hubs to some of Wales' most challenging climbs, these projects will help turn the excitement of the Tour into lasting opportunities for communities. "We want the benefits to be felt long after the race has finished, creating a lasting tourism, sporting and economic legacy for Wales." Ministers say the funding is designed to ensure communities across Wales, including those in Mid Wales, benefit from the international attention generated by the Tour de France, while creating a long-term legacy for tourism, active travel and local businesses. 2027 Tour de France Powis Castle Tour de France Cycling Events Leisure Sport Builth Wells Llandrindod Wells Llanfyllin Machynlleth Newtown Powys Welshpool Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading...
